title: cerastium vulgare var. holosteoides
intro: Cerastium vulgare var. holosteoides, commonly known as mouse-ear chickweed, is a perennial herb in the carnation family (Caryophyllaceae). The plant has been traditionally used for its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties, offering health benefits such as wound healing, skin soothing, and digestive relief. Therapeutically, mouse-ear chickweed is thought to exhibit astringent, demulcent, and vulnerary actions, which help to protect and soothe damaged tissues. The bioactive constituents of Cerastium vulgare var. holosteoides include flavonoids, terpenoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its therapeutic effects.
